page: Microsoft Azure E16-4s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine within the ESv5 series, configured with a constrained core count to provide a high memory-to-vCPU ratio. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V on an x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 4 dedicated vCPUs sourced from 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. The hardware features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for AVX-512 vector extensions and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI instructions.

The primary architectural distinction of this instance is its memory configuration, supplying 128.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 32.0 GB per vCPU. The server does not bundle local storage, requiring network-attached storage options such as Azure Premium SSDs for persistent workloads, and includes zero hardware GPUs. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks register 30.12 GB/sec for read and 25.49 GB/sec for write operations, matching the expected capabilities of this Intel generation.

Benchmark measurements indicate solid single-core metrics, achieving a single-core Geekbench score of 1638.0 and a single-core stress-ng rating of 1895.99. However, aggregate multi-core throughput remains restricted by the 4-vCPU allocation, recording a multi-core Geekbench score of 3526.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 5951.48. In-memory performance reflects this dynamic, with Redis settling at 3.99 million SET operations per second and database operations scoring 2065.72 in PassMark tests.

By constraining the execution environment to 4 vCPUs while retaining a full 128.0 GB memory footprint, the E16-4s_v5 provides a cost-efficient architecture for software platforms licensed on a per-core basis. It is suited for memory-intensive relational databases, caching layers, and enterprise analytics where high RAM capacity is necessary but core-bound compute requirements remain low.
description: Microsoft Azure E16-4s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the ESv5 family engineered for memory-intensive workloads that require lower compute core counts. Powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor, the instance allocates 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, supported by 48 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 instruction sets. It features an expansive 128.0 GB of system memory, providing an elevated ratio of 32.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance bundles no local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage solutions. Performance benchmarks reveal competent single-core metrics alongside moderate multi-threaded throughput, dictated by the core constraint. This hardware balance yields qualitative cost efficiency for systems constrained by per-core software licensing, such as enterprise relational databases, large in-memory caches, and analytics engines.
